summary: Throughput collapse and p99 latency spikes during morning short-stream swarm; evidence of PCIe latency bursts and noisy tenant KV-cache churn
description:
Issue summary: FlowCart (dedicated customer) reports a sharp throughput collapse and prolonged p99 latency spikes across their reserved pool during their peak ingestion window (09:10-09:40 ET) on 2026-03-13. The pattern is repeatable each weekday morning. Impact: sustained failed requests, client timeouts, and downstream backpressure in FlowCart pipelines. Note: this is not an infrastructure-wide outage; affected hosts are concentrated in us-east serving the customer's reserved capacity but cross-tenant interference observed on a subset of GPUs.

High level hypothesis: a burst of many short-lived inference streams from a single tenant is causing persistent slot fragmentation and aggressive KV cache eviction. That, in turn, correlates with brief but recurrent PCIe latency spikes (observed as device IO wait and GPU DMA stalls) which amplify the scheduling delays and cause the autoscaler to overshoot during warmup windows, worsening p99 latency.

Customer visible symptoms: elevated p95/p99 across text generation endpoints, intermittent 5xx stream disconnects, and increased retry traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated FlowCart pool in prod-us-east with tenant pinned model rwd-3b-quantized
2) Generate an artificial workload that opens 500 short streams per minute (each stream sends 1-3 short prompts, then closes) over a 10-minute window
3) Observe scheduler slot allocation, KV cache churn, and GPU IO wait metrics; watch p50/p95/p99 on token generation and overall throughput
4) Compare to a control run with fewer long-lived streams (50 streams with 50 tokens each) — issue does not reproduce under that workload shape
logs:
2026-03-13T09:12:07Z host-312: serving-runtime: batch_worker: GPU DMA stall detected (device_io_wait=420ms)
2026-03-13T09:12:08Z host-312: scheduler: slot_fragmentation=0.78, small_stream_ratio=0.64, pending_queue=312
2026-03-13T09:12:09Z autoscaler: scale_up triggered: +8 slots; observed allocation lag 74s; multiple preemptions logged
2026-03-13T09:13:01Z network: nvlink/pci_util: pcie_latency_spike_ms=360, correlated with increased retry rate from tenant
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: verified customer pool is in dedicated mode and pinned to us-east hosts. Noted strong correlation between short-stream bursts and p99 spikes; reproduced with local load generator.

SRE ran perf captures on two affected hosts: found repeated small-batch dispatches with high DMA latency and elevated gpu_io_wait during burst windows. NVLink/PCIe metrics show short-lived latency bursts (~200-500ms) aligned with KV-cache eviction bursts.

Heap/KV-cache analysis: aggressive eviction rate observed; cache hot set thrashing when many unique prefixes are requested across short streams. This increased CPU-GPU synchronization overhead (small kernel launches) and more PCIe transfers per token.

Autoscaler behavior: reactive policy scaled up based on queue length but allocation lag and subsequent slot fragmenting caused more small-stream dispatches which further worsened contention — feedback loop identified.
No evidence of hardware faults on GPUs (no ECC errors). Affected hosts show normal temps and power; root cause appears workload-pattern-induced IO amplification rather than host failure.
comments: Elena Park (Support): Logged customer's initial report and validated timestamps. Captured request ids and sample payloads from FlowCart.

Aisha Thompson (SRE): Reproduced locally with short-stream swarm; starting isolation steps to throttle noisy tenant at pool edge. Filed scheduler PR proposal to batch short streams together and cap concurrent short-streams per GPU.
Miguel Santos (FlowCart): Confirmed the customer can temporarily shift their job start times; requested a solution that doesn't require app changes.
Raj Patel (Platform Eng): Noted similar signals in unrelated clusters but different root cause; suggested adding PCIe latency metrics to pool health dashboard.
root_cause: Workload shape: sudden multi-tenant short-stream swarm causing high small-batch dispatch frequency, persistent KV cache thrashing, and amplified PCIe/NVLink DMA latency spikes. The autoscaler’s reactive ramp-up and the scheduler's current slot granularity allowed a feedback loop that created sustained contention on a subset of GPUs.
resolution:
Short-term mitigation: applied per-tenant concurrency cap at the pool ingress for FlowCart at 2026-03-13T11:20, which immediately reduced p99 and stabilized throughput. Rolled out an autoscaler policy tweak to add a conservative warmup buffer for dedicated pools during known peak windows.

Long-term fix: merged scheduler change to coalesce many short streams into consolidated micro-batches and to limit concurrent small-streams per GPU (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/4123). Also added a PCIe latency alarm to the pool health dashboard and a runbook entry for noisy-tenant isolation. Patch deployed to canary hosts 2026-03-14 and slated full rollout after validation.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Validate scheduler micro-batching at load across 3 canary clusters (owner: Raj Patel, due: 2026-03-20)
2) Add PCIe/NVLink 1m/5m latency charts to Redwood Console for dedicated pools (owner: Observability team, due: 2026-03-17)
3) Update autoscaler default warmup policy for dedicated pools with high short-stream ratios (owner: Autoscale squad, due: 2026-03-21)
4) Create support playbook snippet to throttle or cordon noisy tenants without a full eviction (owner: Support SRE, due: 2026-03-16)
5) Follow up with FlowCart on workload shaping recommendations and offer help creating a backoff client (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-18)
